How to repot a root bound fern

A fern that has filled its pot will tell you so. Roots circle the inside of the container, push up through the drainage holes and lift the whole plant a little higher each month. Repotting in spring gives it the longest stretch of growth to recover.

Choose the next pot

Pick a pot only one size up, about two fingers wider than the current one. A pot that is much larger holds water around roots that cannot yet reach it, and the damp soil invites rot.

Loosen and trim

Slide the plant out and tease the outer roots apart with your fingers. Snip any that are brown or mushy with clean scissors. Healthy roots are pale and firm, and a few tangled ones are fine.

Settle it in

Add a layer of fresh mix, set the plant at the same depth as before and fill around the sides. Water slowly until it runs from the bottom, then keep the fern out of direct sun for a week.
